chunks: Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Maḥbūb narrated from Mūsā ibn Jaʿfar al-Baghdādī, from ʿAlī ibn Muḥammad ibn Sulaymān al-Nawfalī, who said:

I wrote to Abū Jaʿfar al-Thānī عليه السلام asking him about a land that my grandfather had endowed for the needy among the descendants of so-and-so ibn so-and-so, the man who gathers the tribe, while they are many and scattered through the lands. And among the descendants of the one who made the endowment there is severe need, so they asked me to single them out for it, to the exclusion of the rest of the descendants of the man who gathers the tribe.

So he عليه السلام replied: You mentioned the land which your grandfather endowed for the poor among the descendants of so-and-so. It belongs to those who are present in the town in which the endowment is, and it is not for you to seek out one who is absent.

key_terms.الْمُحْتَاجِينَ: those in need; eligible needy beneficiaries
key_terms.الْوَاقِفِ: the one who made the endowment
key_terms.الْوَقْفُ: the endowed property held as waqf
key_terms.فُقَرَاءِ: the poor among the designated beneficiaries

ai.seo_question: How should an endowment for needy family descendants be distributed when the beneficiaries are scattered across different lands?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning a waqf endowed for needy descendants of a specified family line. Imam Abū Jaʿfar al-Thānī عليه السلام states that the benefit of the endowment is for those present in the locality of the waqf, and that the custodian is not required to search for absent beneficiaries.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.5574 - Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub narrated from Musa ibn Ja'far Al-Baghdadi from Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Sulayman Al-Nawfali, who said:

I wrote to Abu Ja'far Al-Thani (as), peace be upon him, asking about a piece of land that my grandfather had endowed for the needy among the descendants of so-and-so, the man who united the tribe.
However, they are numerous and scattered across different lands, while the descendants of the one who made the endowment are in severe need.
They asked me to allocate the endowment specifically to them, excluding the other descendants of the man who united the tribe.

Imam (as) replied: "You mentioned the land that your grandfather endowed for the poor among the descendants of so-and-so. It is designated for those who are present in the town where the endowment exists, and you are not permitted to seek out those who are absent."
